\begin{lemma}[The cusp neighbourhood and its circle classes]\hypertarget{tag-IP07}{}\label{I:lem:cusp-fundamental-group}
For the cusp neighbourhood $N_0$ and the vanishing lattice
$K=\mathbb Z\langle w,d\rangle$,
\[
 \pi_1(N_0)=\overline\Lambda=\Lambda/K.
 \hypertarget{tag-02P2}{}\label{mapsI:quotient-eq-5}
\]
The punctured-cusp map to this group kills $K$ and the base meridian.
Both long-period covectors extend in integral $H^1(N_0;\mathbb Z)$.
The literal character on an ordinary fibre has no extension to all of
$X\simeq S^6$.
\end{lemma}
input_scope: N_0 is the cusp neighbourhood from the periodic Mumford toric construction, with cocharacter rays (v,1) for v in Z^2, triangulated by the fixed unimodular A2 fan. The small rank-two vanishing lattice is K=Z<w,d>; Lambda is the full marked rank-four period lattice. Long periods induce the residual period action. These are construction data; derive the effect of toric divisor meridians and the base meridian before opening the old paragraph proof. The compact member X is diffeomorphic to S^6.
